the adherence of lymphocytes to the fibroblast mononayer was specific for the PWM-lymphocyte and that this adherence was accompanied by a transformation of the adhering lymphocytes into target-cell lytic cells.
the in vitro differentiated lymphocytes adhered specifically to target cells.
the adherence of lymphocytes to target cells is a process which is specific to the type of lymphocytes and to the nature of the target cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the specific adhesion of lymphocytes to target cells.
a new type of adherence which is specific to the lymphocytes which have been transformed by a specific mitogen.
the study of a lymphocyte transformation which occurs upon the addition of PWM to PHA-, Con A-, or PWM-secondary lymphocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adherence is not a general phenomenon of lymphocyte stimulation, but rather it is specific and characteristic to the secondary lymphocyte population.
the secondary lymphocytes are endowed with specific adherence to target cells and with target-cell lysis.
the adherence of lymphocytes to target cells is mediated through specific receptors on the surface of the lymphocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lymphocyte transformation by PWM is not a random process, but is a highly selective one, which is directed toward the recognition and lysis of target cells.
the secondary lymphocytes which are derived from PHA- and Con A-transformed blast cells and which adhere to fibroblast target cells in vitro are the cells which recognize and lyse these target cells.
in vitro differentiation of lymphocytes into target cell-lytic cells involves specific adherence of the cells to target cells.
